claims.statement: Experience generation, Skill generation, scheduled Experience incubation, and Dream runs all enter review as pending Candidates through ReviewService propose methods; generation itself never approves or publishes an Artifact Revision.

A Candidate is stored as a mutable head plus immutable numbered proposal versions; creation writes version 1 as pending, and revising appends a complete replacement proposal as the next version while advancing the head.

Candidate revise appends a complete immutable proposal as version N+1 and advances the head only when the stored head is still pending at expected_version; otherwise it raises a conflict or terminal error.

The expected_version contract is a compare-and-swap on the pending head: lock_pending updates the head only when candidate_id, artifact kind, version equal expected_version and status equals pending; a mismatch re-reads the head and raises CandidateTerminalError for non-pending status or CandidateConflictError for a stale version.
Candidate status has three values, pending, approved, and rejected; only a pending Candidate can be revised, approved, or rejected, and approved and rejected are terminal.

Approval publishes the reviewed proposal in one database transaction: it creates the Artifact or appends the next Revision under the target identity, updates the Experience or Skill index, and marks the Candidate approved with its exact result_artifact; any failure rolls the whole commit back.

Repeating approval of an already approved Candidate at the same version returns its stored result, while approving a rejected Candidate raises a terminal-state error before target or evidence validation.
Reject moves a pending Candidate to rejected with a decision_reason and never writes an Artifact or Revision.
Revising a Candidate cannot change its target, re-runs proposal-family validation and evidence resolution, and rejects a version that does not match the inspected preview before any write.

Evidence is revalidated at approval and at revision: every exact Source and Artifact reference must exist in the Candidate scope and resolve through the evidence resolver, and a failure-bearing Experience requires a cited failed Task Outcome with verified exact evidence.

An Experience replacement Candidate must identify the exact current target Revision in both target and artifacts; if another approval has already advanced the Artifact head, the stale Candidate is not published and stays pending unless separately rejected.

Direct Create is a separate write path: POST to the scope artifacts collection validates family content, stores a lineage-only Source, and commits the Artifact (including Experience and Skill) through the family writer in one transaction, creating no Candidate.

Direct Replace requires an If-Match ETag equal to the current Artifact revision, writes the next Revision immediately as the current head through the family writer, and creates no Candidate; a stale ETag raises a revision precondition error.

Managed Skill content is canonicalized into a stored instruction package on create, replace, and approval; cached Skill fields must match the exact package, and a mismatched package reference is rejected.

Skill generation validates provenance before proposing: the experience origin requires only Experience references and no target, the source origin requires only exact Source references, and the usage origin requires an exact target Skill plus Source evidence.
An Experience Revision is a situation, action, outcome, and lesson with an optional failure record that carries a recall cue, repair surface, and verification bindings.

Only approved, current Experience heads are eligible for same-scope PreparedContext recall; pending and rejected Candidates and historical Experience Revisions are excluded, and approved managed Skills do not enter PreparedContext.

Experience incubation reads at most EXPERIENCE_INCUBATION_WINDOW_LIMIT (32) Sources from the cursor window when no limit is supplied, and rejects a supplied limit below 1; it sends only task-outcome Sources to the generator and requires every returned candidate to cite Source ids from the current window. When eligible Task Outcomes exist, the pending Candidates, recurrence events, and cursor are written in one transaction, so a failed Candidate write does not advance the cursor. When a window has no eligible Task Outcome, the cursor advances in its own transaction, without a model call and without writing Candidates.
The scheduled Experience incubation job is enabled only by a positive experience schedule interval, and composition requires a configured generation model for it to start.

The recurrence ledger is append-only and idempotent: it is written only inside the Task Outcome incubation window, records selected, avoided, and recurred events, and replaying a window reuses recorded match decisions instead of invoking the generator again.

A recurrence repair proposal is created only when one Experience revision reaches a terminal recurrence streak of at least three on the experience_content repair surface; other repair surfaces produce no Artifact proposal.

Dream-produced Skill Candidates are checked against their originating Dream run and operation at approval, and a revise_skill candidate must still target its original Skill Revision with an unchanged protected metadata set.

Under disabled access mode, review operations do not enforce reviewer identity; under enforced access mode, the scope.reviewer role grants scope.review, and revise additionally requires that the caller is the original proposer.

In enforced access mode, approving an artifact Candidate requires a recorded candidate-owner attestation, otherwise the request fails with artifact_owner_pending; after a successful approval of a Candidate without a target, the resulting Artifact's owner is established from that attestation, while a Candidate that targets an existing Artifact does not change that Artifact's owner.
Approval only writes the Artifact Revision and index state and marks the Candidate approved; it does not install, export, publish, or grant execution authority for a Skill.

The host-local export command fetches one exact Skill Revision and writes it to a new destination directory for Codex or Claude Code; it refuses an existing destination and writes a powercontext.json manifest recording the exact Artifact reference and a SHA-256 of the rendered SKILL.md.
For package-backed Skills, the export downloads the exact archive, rebuilds its package reference, and refuses to materialize it unless that reference matches the stored Skill Artifact package.

Local Skill publication inspection classifies a target as unpublished, current, update_available, drifted, conflict, or incompatible from the destination files and the stored publication row; a directory the publication does not own is reported as a conflict and is never replaced. The pending and delivery_failed states of the same enum come from the remote distribution path.

Managed publication to a configured Agent target records a per-target publication intent before materializing files: the first publication creates the publication row at generation 0, an identical intent reuses the stored row without advancing it, and a changed intent replaces the row through replacement CAS that checks the expected generation and advances it by one. The observed local result is then written through observation CAS, which checks the expected generation without advancing it.

Remote Skill distribution keeps server-owned desired state per target; reconciliation returns only actions for the latest publication generation, download serves only the exact currently desired package, and a Receipt older than the stored generation is rejected as stale.

The Receiver applies reconciliation actions locally, records a Receipt after the local change, keeps signed journals for replay, and keeps a failed Receipt delivery pending instead of mutating the host again.

Unpublish of a managed Skill publication stages the existing destination directory aside, advances the publication generation through replacement CAS, and restores the staged directory if the database update fails.

In the publication replacement CAS, the UPDATE matches the stored row's scope, target, artifact and expected generation, and writes generation as expected_generation + 1; when the update does not match exactly one row, a missing row raises RepositoryNotFoundError and a stale generation raises StoredPayloadConflictError.

An explicit Experience merge creates a new identity from at least two distinct exact input reads; each input must be active, must not already be merged, and must still match its frozen revision and state version, otherwise the merge fails with a conflict or invalid-state error. Each input becomes deprecated with merged_into_id set to the new result, and the result is written active with the inputs as lineage.

Forget deprecates one exact current active Artifact without a replacement and without a new content Revision; it requires the expected revision and state version, and writes nothing when the Artifact is already deprecated.

Restore and undo_merge follow the merged_into chain from the target to its endpoint; undo_merge and restoring an input retire the merge results on that path and reactivate their frozen inputs; a retired identity cannot be restored and a live path cannot end in a retired result.

Restore previews are signed with the shared key configured by atomic_memory_preview_signing_secret; without that key, preview and token validation fail with invalid_preview, and the preview token lifetime defaults to 300 seconds with a maximum of 3600.

A restore without a preview token retries commit conflicts up to restore_retry_budget, which defaults to 3, and then raises; a restore with a preview token reports a conflict as a stale-preview error without retrying.

The Experience merge adapter accepts only direct Sources and exact in-Scope Artifacts as lineage, rejects publication lineage on new writes, and updates the Experience index for each published merge result; composition registers this adapter as the Experience merge service.
When the Experience generator returns no proposal, generation returns an empty result and creates no Candidate.

When an approval loses a race (artifact target conflict, terminal state, or revision conflict), the approve wrapper re-reads the Candidate: a rejected Candidate raises a terminal error, an approved Candidate at the expected version returns its stored result, and any other state re-raises the original error.

In enforced access mode, each Experience or Skill proposal or generation attests the request principal as the candidate owner after it is committed; with access disabled, no candidate-owner attestation is recorded.

In enforced access mode, approve and revise on a Candidate with a target additionally require write authority on the target Artifact, while reject requires only the scope.review permission on the scope.

In enforced access mode, artifact Candidate responses carry permission flags computed from scope.review and the candidate-owner attestation: can_reject requires a pending Candidate and scope.review, can_approve additionally requires an attestation, and can_revise additionally requires that the caller is the recorded proposer.

The Skill Receiver's sync first replays signed journals for undelivered receipts and returns without reconciling while any receipt is still pending; only when none is pending does it request reconciliation from the Server.

Remote Skill publish requires an active target and a package-backed Skill; a retired Skill is refused, and a deprecated Skill is refused unless allow_deprecated is set. A first publication creates a pending desired row at generation 0, and an identical desired state returns the stored row unchanged, while a changed desired state replaces it as pending through replacement CAS.

Local managed Skill publish requires allow_managed_publish on the Agent target, refuses incompatible Skills, refuses retired Skills, refuses deprecated Skills unless allow_deprecated is set, and proceeds only when the observed state is unpublished or update_available; any other observed state raises a conflict.
Artifact governance defines three lifecycle states, active, deprecated, and retired, stored separately from immutable Artifact Revisions.
